Rashi on Ketubot 22a:11:1.english: She said, "I am ritually impure" - She said to her husband, "I am a menstruant."

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:11:2.english: I am pure - I was not a menstruant.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:1.hebrew: תרי ותרי נינהו - כי אמרי לא גזל, הוו להו תרי ותרי ולא מתכשר בהכי, דקי"ל לקמן בפרקין (כתובות דף כו.), אין ערער פחות משנים:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:1.english: They are two and two - When [the witnesses] say [that] he did not steal, they are two [against] two, and he is not rendered fit thereby, for we hold later in our chapter (Ketubot 26a) [that] a challenge is [made by] no fewer than two [witnesses].

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:2.hebrew: דפגם משפחה - שהעידו עליו שהוא עבד, ועבד פסול לדין ולעדות ק"ו מאשה, כדאמר בפ' החובל (ב"ק פח.):
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:2.english: Of flawed lineage - That they testified about him that he is a slave, and a slave is disqualified from judging and from testifying a fortiori from a woman, as is stated in the chapter [entitled] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 88a).

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:3.hebrew: גלוי מילתא בעלמא הוא - משחתמו, אמאי אין מעידין עליו? מאי חשד נוגע בעדות איכא הכא? דבר זה צריכין הן לברר, ודבר העשוי לגלות הוא, שיבדקו אחריו עד שיבורר הדבר. ואין עדותן של אלו תלוי בהגדתן, ואינן אלא מגלי דבר בעלמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:3.english: It is a mere revealing of a matter - Once they have signed, why may they not testify about him? What suspicion of being an interested party in the testimony is there here? They must clarify this matter, and it is a matter that is bound to be revealed, for they will investigate him until the matter is clarified. Thus, the testimony of these [judges] does not depend on their declaration, and they are merely revealing a matter.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:1:4.english: That he repented - And returned the stolen property.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:2:1.english: And if it were not for Rabbi Abba of Akko - Who reminded me of it after some time.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:2:3.english: And one of them died - Before they signed [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:2:4.hebrew: צריכין למיכתב כו' - דקיום השטר בשלשה, והרואה שנים חתומין בו יאמר שבשנים קיימוהו:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:2:4.english: They must write, etc. - For the ratification of a document [requires] three [judges], and one who sees two signed on it will say that they ratified it with two.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:3:1.english: And if [one] wrote in it: "This document was produced before us, the court," [it] is no longer necessary - For fewer than three [judges] are not called "a court."

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:4:1.hebrew: בי דינא דרבנא אשי - אורחא דמילתא נקט, שהוא היה ראש ישיבה במתא מחסיא בימי רב נחמן בר יצחק, דהוא מרא דשמעתא, דודאי בי דינא דרב אשי לא עבדין בתרין:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:4:1.english: The court of our teacher Rav Ashi - [The Gemara] mentions a typical case, as he was head of the academy in Mata Mechasya in the days of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, who is the author of the statement — for certainly the court of Rav Ashi would not act with two [judges].

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:4:2.hebrew: ואמר לנא רבנא אשי - לאזדקוקי ליה ולקיומי, דכיון דרב אשי גופיה הזקיקן, איהו ודאי לתלתא אמר. ויש מפרשין: ״ואמר לנא רבנא אשי״ תלתא נינהו. ולא נהירא לי, דאי רב אשי חד מנהון, מאי ״ואמר לנא״ דכתבי ביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:4:2.english: And our teacher Rav Ashi said to us - To attend to it and ratify [it]; for since Rav Ashi himself instructed them [to do so], he certainly spoke to three [judges]. And some explain: "and our teacher Rav Ashi said to us" [indicates that] they are three. But this does not seem right to me, for if Rav Ashi was one of them, what is [the meaning of] "and [he] said to us" that they wrote in it?

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:5:1.english: I was taken captive - among idolaters.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:5:2.english: And I am pure - [Meaning] that I was not cohabited with by an idolater.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:5:3.english: She is deemed credible - and is permitted to [marry] a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:5:4.english: And if after she married, witnesses came - In the Gemara it explains to which [clause] this refers.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:6:1.hebrew: נתתי לאיש אסרה - לכל העולם, דלא ידעינן למאן, וכי אמר הזה, התירה לו:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:6:1.english: I gave [my daughter] to the man — he rendered her forbidden - to everyone, since we do not know to whom [he gave her]; and when he says "this [man]," he rendered her permitted to him.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:7:1.hebrew: שנאמן לאסור את בתו - כשהיא קטנה או נערה, שבידו לקדשה, כדאמרי' בפ' נערה שנתפתתה: מנין שאם אמר "קדשתיה לפלוני", שהוא נאמן לאוסרה על הכל:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:7:1.english: That [a father] is deemed credible to render his daughter forbidden - When she is a minor or a na'arah, where it is in his power to betroth her, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah Shenitpatah: From where [is it derived] that if he said, "I betrothed her to so-and-so," he is deemed credible to render her forbidden to everyone?

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:7:2.hebrew: את בתי נתתי - אלמא בדידיה תליא נתינה, והימניה קרא למימר הכי:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:7:2.english: I gave my daughter - Thus, the giving [in marriage] depends on him, and the verse deemed him credible to say so.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:7:3.english: "This" — why do I [need it] - Since it is not needed for [the principle of] "the mouth that forbade."

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:8:1.hebrew: ולא ליבם - אם הוציא שם רע על נישואי אחיו, שאין היבם נידון כמוציא שם רע ליענש במאה כסף, והכי מוכח לקמן בפרק נערה:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:8:1.english: And not to the yavam - If he brought an evil report regarding his brother's marriage, for the yavam is not judged as a defamer to be penalized one hundred [shekels of] silver, and so it is proven later in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah.

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:9:1.english: Amatla [a rationale] - An explanation and a reason why she initially said, "I am betrothed."

Rashi on Ketubot 22a:9:2.hebrew: אם נתנה אמתלא לדבריה נאמנת - הואיל ונתנה אמתלא, נאמנת:
Rashi on Ketubot 22a:9:2.english: If she provided a rationale for her words, she is deemed credible - Since she provided a rationale, she is deemed credible.

Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:1:1.hebrew: תרי ותרי נינהו - פירש בקונטרס: וכי אמרי לא גזל, הוו להו תרי ותרי, ולא מתכשר בהכי. וקשה, דהכא אליבא דרב הונא קיימינן, דאית ליה (שבועות דף מז:) דזו באה בפני עצמה ומעידה, דאית לן למימר "אוקי גברא אחזקתיה"! ועוד, דלרב חסדא דאמר (שם) "בהדי סהדי שקרי למה לי", מודה הכא דהאי גברא ממילא מתכשר; שהרי אם כת אחת מאלו מעידה על אדם אחד שהוא פסול, לרב חסדא דחשיב להו סהדי שקרי לא היתה נאמנת אע"ג דאין אדם מכחישה, וכ"ש היכא דאיכא סהדי דמכחשי, דלא מהימני. וע"ק לר"י, דקאמר "אי ערער דפגם משפחה גלוי מילתא בעלמא הוא", ופי' הקונט' דדבר העשוי ליגלות הוא, שיבדקו עד שיתברר הדבר. וזהו תימה: איך יתברר הדבר לעולם? כיון שאלו ב' אומרים שהוא עבד, אין כל העולם יכולים להכחישן, דתרי כמאה! על כן נראה כפר"ח, דלא איירי בעדות דיינין אלא בעדות אחרים, וה"פ: אם עד שלא חתמו קרא ערער על אחד מהם, מעידים שנים מן השוק עליו וחותם, דהוי כאילו ישבו בית דין אחר שהכשירוהו, ולא בטל וועד המושב, וחותמין. משחתמו השנים ולא הספיק השלישי לחתום עד שקרא עליו ערער, בא ערער וביטל וועד המושב של אותו ב"ד; אע"פ שאחרי כן העידו אחרים שהוא כשר, כיון שביטל ההוא מושב, בטל, וצריך לחזור ולהושיב ב"ד על כך. ערער דמאי? אי ערער דגזלנותא — תרי ותרי נינהו, ולא מיפסיל, דאוקי תרי בהדי תרי ואוקי גברא אחזקתיה; וכיון דאיגלאי מלתא דמעולם לא היה פסול, הרי לא היה בטל וועד המושב של אותו ב"ד. אי ערער דפגם משפחה, שאמרו עליו שהוא עבד, ואלו מזימים אותם — דאי אומרים שאינו עבד, א"כ היה נפסל, דליכא למימר אוקי גברא אחזקה, דאם הוא עבד לא היה לו חזקת כשרות מעולם — א"כ גלוי מילתא בעלמא הוא, דכיון דאיגלאי מלתא דכשר היה, מה איכפת לן בההוא ערעור? ולא בטל וועד המושב. לעולם ערער דגזלנותא, ודקאמרי הנך סהדי "ידעינן ביה דעבד תשובה" — וכיון דמודו לקמאי דגזלן הוא, הוה ערער דידהו ערער ובטל וועד המושב, דהואיל ואמת הוא שנפסל, הוי בחזקת פסלות עד שנודע לנו כשרותו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:1:1.english: They are two and two - Rashi explained: And when they say he did not steal, they are two [witnesses] against two, and he is not rendered fit through this. And this is difficult, for here we are standing according to Rav Huna, who holds (Shevuot 47b) that each [pair] comes on its own and testifies, so we must say, "Establish the person on his presumptive status." And furthermore, even according to Rav Chisda, who said (there), "Why do I need [to rely on] false witnesses?", he agrees here that this person is automatically rendered fit; for if one of these pairs testifies about a person that he is disqualified, according to Rav Chisda — who considers them false witnesses — it would not be believed even though no one contradicts it, and all the more so where there are witnesses who contradict [them], that they are not believed. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak has an additional difficulty: for [the Gemara] says, "If it is a challenge of flawed lineage, it is a mere revealing of a matter," and Rashi explained that it is something destined to be revealed, so they investigate until the matter is clarified. And this is astonishing: how will the matter ever be clarified? Since these two say that he is a slave, the entire world cannot contradict them, for two are like a hundred! Therefore, it appears like the explanation of Rabbeinu Chananel, that [the Gemara] is not speaking of the testimony of judges, but rather of the testimony of others, and this is its explanation: If before they signed, a challenge arose against one of them, two [witnesses] from the market testify about him and he signs, for it is as if another court sat and declared him fit, and the session of the court is not invalidated, and they sign. Once the two have signed, and the third did not manage to sign before a challenge arose against him, a challenge has come and invalidated the session of that court; even if afterward others testified that he is fit, since that session was invalidated, it is void, and it is necessary to reconvene a court for this. What kind of challenge? If it is a challenge of theft — they are two against two, and he is not disqualified, for we set two against two and establish the person on his presumptive status; and since it is revealed that he was never disqualified, the session of that court was not invalidated. If it is a challenge of flawed lineage, where they said about him that he is a slave, and these [other witnesses] render them zomemim — for if they [merely] say that he is not a slave, then he would be disqualified, as one cannot say "establish the person on his presumptive status," since if he is a slave he never had a presumptive status of fitness — then it is a mere revealing of a matter, for since it is revealed that he was fit, what do we care about that challenge? And the session of the court is not invalidated. Actually, it is a challenge of theft, and as for what those witnesses say, "We know about him that he repented" — since they admit to the first [witnesses] that he was a thief, their challenge is a [valid] challenge and the session of the court is invalidated, for since it is true that he was disqualified, he is in a presumptive state of disqualification until his fitness becomes known to us.

Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:2:1.hebrew: במותב תלתא כחדא הוינא וחד ליתוהי - פירוש: צריך לכתוב "וחד ליתוהי", כיון דכתב בהדיא "במותב תלתא הוינא" ואין חותמין בו כי אם שנים; אבל ודאי אם לא כתב "וחד ליתוהי" — כשר. תדע מדקאמר: "ואי כתב ביה בי דינא תו לא צריך", ומיירי דלא כתב "וחד ליתוהי", מדפריך: "ודלמא ב"ד חצוף הוה":
Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:2:1.english: "We were [convened] in a session of three together, and one is no longer [alive]" - Explanation: One must write "and one is no longer [alive]," since it explicitly wrote "we were [convened] in a session of three" and only two sign on it; however, certainly if one did not write "and one is no longer [alive]," it is valid. You can know [this] from what [the Gemara] says: "And if it wrote in it 'court,' it no longer needs [anything further]," and it is speaking of a case where it did not write "and one is no longer [alive]," as [evidenced by the fact that] it asks: "And perhaps it was an impudent court?"

Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:4:1.hebrew: ודלמא רבנן דבי רב אשי כשמואל סבירא להו - פי': כמו שסובר שמואל בעלמא, כן סבירא להו בקיום שטרות. אבל שמואל מצי סבר שפיר דבקיום שטרות בעי ג', דהא רב נחמן סבר לה כשמואל בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ג. ושם) דשנים שדנו דיניהם דין, ורב נחמן גופיה סבר דקיום שטרות בשלשה בפ' חזקת הבתים (ב"ב מ.) גבי ג' ארצות לחזקה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:4:1.english: And perhaps the Rabbis of the court of Rav Ashi hold like Shmuel - Explanation: Just as Shmuel holds in general [that two judges are valid], so they hold regarding the ratification of documents. However, Shmuel himself could well hold that ratification of documents requires three [judges], for Rav Nachman holds like Shmuel in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (3a and there) that when two [judges] judged, their judgment is valid, yet Rav Nachman himself holds that ratification of documents is [performed] with three [judges], in the chapter Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 40a) regarding three lands for chazakah.

Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:6:1.hebrew: מנין להפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר מן התורה שנאמר את בתי נתתי לאיש וגו' - משמע דאין האב נאמן להתיר את בתו כשאסרה אלא מחמת מגו. ותימה: דאם בא אחד ואמר "קדשתי את בתי", ולאחר שעה או למחר אמר "לפלוני קדשתיה", לא יהא נאמן, כיון דהשתא ליכא מגו? ואומר ר"י, דבענין זה, שאינו סותר דבריו הראשונים ולא בא אלא לפרש דבריו הראשונים, מהימן, אע"ג דליכא מגו. והכא דריש מ"את בתי" הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר, כגון דקאי האיש שקידש לו קמיה וקאמר "את בתי נתתי לאיש" ושתיק, דמשמע ודאי שאינו מכיר שזה חתנו, מדלא אמר "את בתי נתתי לזה" או "לאיש הזה" ביחד בלא הפסק מרובה; הלכך לא יהא נאמן אחר כך אלא תוך כדי דבור, דאיכא מגו. ועוד אומר ר"י, דאיכא למימר אפילו בכה"ג מהימן בלא מגו, וקרא יתירא קדריש; ואם אינו ענין כאן — דאפילו לאחר זמן נאמן, דסברא הוא שיהא נאמן לפרש למי נתנה, אע"פ שלא פירש מתחלה שלא היה חושש לפרש — תנהו ענין להיכא דאינו נאמן לאחר זמן, שיהא נאמן בתוך כדי דבור במגו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:6:1.english: "From where [do we derive] 'the mouth that prohibited is the mouth that permitted' from the Torah? As it is stated: 'I gave my daughter to a man,' etc." - This implies that a father is not believed to permit his daughter after he has prohibited her except by virtue of migo [since he could have remained silent]. And [this is] surprising: if someone came and said, "I betrothed my daughter," and after an hour or the next day he said, "I betrothed her to so-and-so," would he not be believed, since now there is no migo? And R. Yitzchak says that in such a case, where he does not contradict his initial statement and comes only to clarify his initial statement, he is believed, even though there is no migo. And here [the Gemara] expounds from "I gave my daughter..." [the principle of] "the mouth that prohibited is the mouth that permitted" [in a case] such as where the man to whom he betrothed her is standing before him, and he says, "I gave my daughter to a man," and falls silent — which certainly implies that he does not recognize that this [man] is his son-in-law, since he did not say, "I gave my daughter to this [man]" or "to this man" together without a substantial pause; therefore, he would not be believed afterward except within tokh kedei dibbur [the time required for a brief utterance], where there is migo. And R. Yitzchak says further that one can say that even in such a case he is believed without migo, and [the Gemara] is expounding a superfluous verse; and if it has no application here — since he is believed even after some time, as it is logical that he should be believed to clarify to whom he gave her, even though he did not specify initially because he did not care to specify — apply it to a case where he is not believed after some time, [teaching] that he is believed within tokh kedei dibbur with migo.

Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:7:1.hebrew: [מנין לאב שנאמן לאסור וכו' - תימה: מה צריך קרא? תיפוק ליה דנאמן הואיל ובידו לקדשה, כדאמר ביש נוחלין (ב"ב קלד:): בעל שאמר "גרשתי את אשתי" — נאמן הואיל ובידו לגרשה. וי"ל דהכא אין בידו כל כך, דשמא לא ימצא אדם שיקדשנה (כדאיתא קדושין סד.); להכי איצטריך קרא. ומיהו, אם אמר על בתו בוגרת "קדשתיה כשהיתה נערה או קטנה", נראה דאינו נאמן, דהשתא אין בידו כלל. דאף על גב דלקמן בפ' נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות דף מו.) פריך: "ואימא הנ"מ קטנה, אבל נערה איהי תיקדש נפשה" — לפי זה היה צ"ל דנאמן לאסור אפילו בשעה שאין בידו לקדשה, דקרא בנערה כתיב ובעי למימר דאין בידו לקדשה ו"את בתי נתתי" כשהיתה קטנה, וגזרת הכתוב הוא דנאמן אע"פ שאין בידו — אבל לפי המסקנא לא נאמר כן]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 22a:7:1.english: [From where [is it derived] that a father is deemed credible to render [his daughter] forbidden, etc. - This is surprising: why is a verse needed? Derive it from the fact that he is deemed credible since it is in his power to betroth her, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 134b): A husband who said, "I divorced my wife," is deemed credible since it is in his power to divorce her! One can answer that here it is not so much in his power, because perhaps he will not find a man who will betroth her (as it is [stated] in Kiddushin 64a); therefore, a verse is necessary. However, if he said regarding his adult daughter (bogeret), "I betrothed her when she was a na'arah or a minor," it appears that he is not deemed credible, since now it is not in his power at all. For even though later in the chapter Na'arah Shenitpattah (Ketubot 46a) [the Gemara] asks: "And say that this applies [only to] a minor, whereas a na'arah may betroth herself" — according to that [premise], one would have to say that he is deemed credible to render [her] forbidden even at a time when it is not in his power to betroth her, since the verse is written regarding a na'arah and [the Gemara] wants to say that it is not in his power to betroth her and [that] "I gave my daughter" [refers to] when she was a minor, and [thus] it is a scriptural decree that he is deemed credible even though it is not in his power — nevertheless, according to the conclusion [of that sugya], this is not said].
